title: School event catering briefs: access, timing and dietary needs
body_markdown:
A school event catering brief in Dubai is a written plan that tells a caterer who needs feeding, when food must be served, how the campus can be accessed and which dietary requirements apply. For school organisers, the key is to coordinate catering with pupil supervision, visitor procedures and the event timetable—not simply choose a menu.


**TL;DR**

- A school event catering brief Dubai organisers can use should define access, serving times, dietary requirements and responsibilities.
- myCHEF provides event catering with vetted chefs; confirm the proposed scope against your school's requirements.
- Choose delivery, staffed service or live cooking according to campus facilities and supervision arrangements.
- Ask for written dietary handling arrangements rather than relying on menu names or verbal assurances.


## Why a clear catering brief matters for schools

A school event brings together audiences with different needs: pupils, parents, teachers, visiting speakers and support staff. A meal served during a scheduled break requires a different plan from refreshments available throughout a family celebration.

Your brief connects those needs to practical arrangements. Security needs the arrival details. Facilities staff need the equipment requirements. The event lead needs to know who will manage service and clear the area afterwards.

Start by separating event catering from an ongoing school meal programme. This guide covers a defined occasion, such as a school fair, staff gathering, graduation reception or parent event. For a broader comparison of providers, the [Dubai catering companies guide](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-catering-companies-in-dubai) provides a next step alongside your written brief.

**myCHEF catering is an option for school event organisers seeking a catering service with vetted chefs.** Suitability still depends on the proposed menu, staffing, campus arrangements and the school's approval process. A catering enquiry is not confirmation that every requirement has been accepted.

## How to write a school event catering brief

Build the brief in a shared document before requesting proposals. The school should own the attendance figures, campus instructions and event schedule; the caterer should explain how the proposed service will work within them.

### Define the audience and event format

State what the occasion is and who will eat. Avoid sending only a total attendance figure: adults attending a reception and younger pupils eating during a supervised break need different menu and service discussions.

Separate invited attendance from confirmed meal numbers. Explain whether guests will arrive together, move through the event gradually or eat in assigned groups. Include the arrangements for teachers and support staff rather than treating them as an afterthought.

An **illustrative planning example** is an event with 90 pupils eating in 3 groups of 30 pupils. Those figures describe the organiser's proposed schedule, not a recommended catering capacity. The caterer must assess staffing and service requirements against the actual menu and space.

Close this part of the brief with:

- Event purpose and named school contact.
- Pupil age groups and adult attendance, recorded separately.
- Confirmed meal numbers and the deadline for revisions.
- Meal occasion: breakfast, lunch, refreshments or reception.
- Grouped service, seated dining or open attendance.

### Map the campus access and catering space

Walk the route yourself with the school's facilities or security contact. Record the approved entrance, unloading point and route to the service area. A location pin alone does not explain which gate a delivery team should use.

Describe the space as it exists, not as you expect it to work. Tell the caterer whether preparation facilities, refrigeration, handwashing facilities, power and water are available for their use. Ask the caterer to confirm what they need and what they will bring.

For an outdoor event in Dubai, include shade, equipment placement and an alternative location in the planning discussion. Do not assume that a supplier can cook anywhere on campus or that the school's kitchen is available.

Give the caterer:

- Approved gate, unloading location and arrival contact.
- School-issued visitor and supplier access instructions.
- Route restrictions, stairs, lifts and trolley access.
- Confirmed facilities available for catering use.
- Service-area layout and agreed indoor alternative.

### Fix the service windows and handover points

Start with the school timetable. Work backwards from the moment guests should receive food, then ask the caterer to propose arrival, setup and readiness times. Avoid inventing a standard setup allowance before the supplier has reviewed the scope.

Write each timing as a distinct milestone. Arrival is not the same as readiness, and readiness is not the same as the first serving. Identify who authorises service to begin if an assembly, performance or registration period runs late.

myCHEF provides catering for events; you can submit this written timetable as part of an enquiry rather than starting with an unstructured menu discussion. Ask for a proposed service plan and check it against campus operations before accepting it.

Include:

- Supplier arrival and access window.
- Setup completion and school handover time.
- Serving windows for each audience or group.
- Named person authorised to approve schedule changes.
- Service finish, clearing and departure arrangements.

### Record dietary requirements and handling expectations

Use the school's approved process to collect dietary information. Distinguish allergies from intolerances, religious requirements and preferences. A vegetarian choice does not answer every dietary question, and a dish name does not establish its ingredients or preparation arrangements.

Share the catering information the supplier needs through an appropriate school-approved channel. Where individual meals need identification, agree a discreet labelling and handover method that works with the school's supervision arrangements.

**Ask for written answers about ingredients, substitutions and cross-contact handling.** Do not describe a meal as suitable for a particular allergy unless the caterer has confirmed the relevant requirements and the school has reviewed that response. Keep the school's existing emergency procedures separate from the catering brief.

Record:

- Dietary meal counts and the process for confirming them.
- School restrictions on ingredients brought onto campus.
- Ingredient information and agreed meal identification.
- Preparation, transport and serving arrangements for dietary meals.
- Substitution approval and pupil handover responsibilities.

### Assign staffing, equipment and clearing responsibilities

Decide what your school can realistically manage before choosing a service format. A delivery proposal leaves different tasks with the organiser from a staffed proposal. Neither description tells you everything without an itemised scope.

Ask who will receive the food, set out the service area, replenish dishes and remove waste. Confirm separately who supervises pupils and controls queues. Do not assume catering staff will take on school supervision duties.

For myCHEF catering, request the staffing and equipment details for the proposed event rather than assuming a standard package. The business provides catering and vetted chefs, but the accepted proposal must establish the actual responsibilities for your occasion.

Specify:

- School lead and catering lead for the event.
- Receiving, setup and food-service responsibilities.
- Tables, serving equipment, crockery and cutlery ownership.
- Queue management and pupil supervision responsibilities.
- Waste removal, equipment collection and final handover.

### Compare proposals against the same brief

Send the same document to every shortlisted caterer. Ask each supplier to identify inclusions, exclusions, assumptions and anything that requires a site discussion. This gives you a clearer comparison than differently structured menu quotations.

Look beyond food selection. Compare staffing, transport, equipment, service duration, dietary arrangements and clearing. These are scope and price drivers; ask for them to be itemised rather than assuming the headline quotation includes them.

Before approval, return unresolved questions to the supplier and obtain a revised written scope. Give the school and caterer one agreed version, with a named owner for subsequent changes.

Check:

- Menu and quantities against the confirmed attendance.
- Staffing, equipment and transport included in the proposal.
- Dietary requirements accepted and any stated limitations.
- Timing, access and clearing responsibilities.
- Revision deadlines and approval arrangements.

## Which catering format suits your school event?

**Choose the format your school can support, not the most elaborate presentation.** The options below are formats to discuss with prospective suppliers, not confirmed packages or inclusions from myCHEF.

| Option | Best for | Practical advantage | Key limitation |
|---|---|---|---|
| Drop-off catering | Staff meetings or events with an organised school receiving team | Separates food delivery from the school's event management | The school must agree who handles setup, service and clearing |
| Staffed buffet | Family events with an agreed service area and queue plan | Gives the supplier a defined role in serving and replenishment | Needs space, staffing detail and clear pupil supervision boundaries |
| Individually packed meals | Grouped pupil service with an agreed distribution system | Allows meals to be allocated through a planned handover | Dietary identification, packaging and waste handling need attention |
| Seated service | Formal receptions with assigned seating | Connects the meal to a controlled event schedule | Requires an agreed table plan and coordination of service |
| Live cooking | Events with suitable facilities and school-approved cooking arrangements | Makes food preparation part of the event format | Adds equipment, access and operational requirements |

For a simple delivery-led event, the [drop-off catering guide](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-drop-off-catering-services-in-dubai) offers a related comparison. Use it alongside your school's receiving and supervision plan, not instead of one.

A quick way to narrow the format is to assess **Audience**, **Facilities**, **Timing** and **Responsibilities** together. A menu that works for the audience still needs a suitable space and a workable handover.


![Catering format linked to audience, facilities, timing and responsibilities](https://gwvckixiegkllthleuyt.supabase.co/storage/v1/object/public/workspace-article-images-public/fa020181-58a1-4f11-bd05-244a75273f40/body-a49fe3bf16c6ccb494f24d01b213af8e.jpg)

*Choose the service format after checking the school's practical arrangements.*


## What should the final brief contain?

Keep the main brief easy to scan. Attach the campus plan and detailed dietary information separately where appropriate, using the school's approved sharing process. The working document should show the version date and the person authorised to approve changes.

A useful brief has these fields:

- **Event:** occasion, date, location and school organiser.
- **Attendance:** pupil groups, adults and confirmed meal counts.
- **Menu:** meal format, proposed dishes and required ingredient information.
- **Dietary needs:** counts, identification method and agreed handling arrangements.
- **Access:** gate, unloading point, visitor instructions and arrival contact.
- **Timing:** arrival, readiness, serving, clearing and departure.
- **Scope:** staffing, equipment, school responsibilities and exclusions.

Do not use a sample menu as proof of dietary suitability. If you include illustrative dishes, mark them as proposals and ask the caterer to confirm ingredients, preparation and substitutions before approval.

## Common mistakes in school catering briefs

### Giving one attendance total

A combined total hides differences between pupil meals, parent refreshments and staff catering. Break attendance into the groups that need different food or service arrangements.

### Treating delivery as a staffed service

Food arriving at the gate does not establish who will carry it inside, set it out or serve it. Record the receiving contact and every task that remains with the school.

### Leaving dietary checks until menu approval

A menu agreed before dietary information is collected creates another round of decisions. Establish requirements early, then confirm the supplier's written response before final approval.

### Assuming campus access is straightforward

The correct building address is not enough. Share school-issued arrival instructions and check that the supplier understands the unloading route and access window.

### Changing the timetable without updating the caterer

A delayed performance or revised pupil grouping changes the service plan. Nominate one school contact to communicate changes and obtain the supplier's acknowledgement.

## FAQ


**What should I include in a school event catering brief in Dubai?**

Include the event date, campus location, audience, meal counts, service windows, dietary requirements and access instructions. Specify who provides equipment, supervises pupils, serves food and clears the area.

**Which catering format is best for a school event?**

The best format is the one that matches your school's facilities, timetable and available staff. Compare delivery, staffed service, packed meals and other proposed formats against the same written requirements.

**Can we use drop-off catering for a pupil event?**

Assess drop-off catering against the school's receiving, serving and supervision arrangements. Confirm who takes delivery, distributes meals, manages dietary identification and handles clearing before approving the proposal.

**How should a school share dietary requirements with a caterer?**

Use the school's approved information-sharing process and provide the details required to plan the meals. Ask for written confirmation of ingredients, meal identification, substitutions and cross-contact handling arrangements.

**How much does school event catering cost?**

Request an itemised quotation based on the event brief. Menu, meal numbers, staffing, equipment, transport, service duration and clearing responsibilities determine the scope you need to compare.

**What access details does a school caterer need?**

Provide the approved entrance, unloading point, arrival contact and route to the catering area. Add school-issued visitor instructions and confirm which facilities the catering team is authorised to use.

**Can myCHEF cater for a school event?**

myCHEF provides event catering with vetted chefs. Submit the school event details and ask for confirmation of the menu, staffing, dietary arrangements and campus requirements for the proposed service.


## One final check before approval

Ask someone outside the organising team to read the brief and explain who receives the delivery, who serves the dietary meals and who authorises a delayed start. If the answers require a separate conversation, add them to the document.

**The final brief should make responsibilities visible, not leave them to be inferred.** Keep the agreed version available to the school lead and catering lead on the event day.

## Related guides

- [Corporate lunch catering options](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-corporate-lunch-catering-companies-in-dubai) for school staff lunches and meetings.
- [Vegan catering options](https://www.mychef.ae/blog/best-vegan-catering-services-in-dubai) for a separate look at plant-based menu planning.

For a tailored myCHEF enquiry, send the event date, school location, pupil and adult guest counts, and the service required. Include the proposed serving windows, campus access instructions and dietary requirements so the catering discussion starts with a clear brief.
